# A US vendor's bill for one litre of fuel, expensed to an account kept to
# thousandths.
#
# Fuel is priced to a tenth of a cent, so the expense account is denominated
# at 1/1000 rather than at the cent — GnuCash keeps that per account and this
# tool round-trips it as `commodity_scu:` (see account_with_finer_scu.txt).
#
# The figure *stated* is a whole number of cents, because that is all a file
# may state: a booked amount is judged against the currency however fine the
# account is. This read 1.819 before, and what a sub-cent booked amount bought
# was a split whose amount sat at the account's unit while its value was
# rounded to the currency's — one split carrying two figures for one sum.
#
# The account's unit still matters here, which is the point of the fixture:
# the bill is in USD, so the payable credit is a cost basis priced through
# this CAD split, and applying the transaction's rate back to it has to round
# the way the split is held — to the thousandth — or a correct book reads as
# converted at two rates over a difference smaller than a cent.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_verify_costs.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses:Fuel
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
	commodity_scu: 1000
2026-01-01 open Liabilities
	type: Liability
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD
	type: Accounts Payable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"

2026-01-10 * "One litre of fuel from a US vendor, at 1.4 CAD/USD"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Expenses:Fuel 1.82 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		value: "1.30"
	Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD -1.30 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		value: "-1.30"
